## Datasets

```{r datasets }

library(ggplot2)
library(AICcmodavg)

species <- read.csv('/Users/meganyoumans/Desktop/Adelphi Coursework/Statistical Modeling/Datasets 2/Datasets/species.csv')
bolger <- read.csv('/Users/meganyoumans/Desktop/Adelphi Coursework/Statistical Modeling/Datasets 2/Datasets/bolger.csv')
molerat <- read.csv('/Users/meganyoumans/Desktop/Adelphi Coursework/Statistical Modeling/Datasets 2/Datasets/molerat.csv')

```

## Species Poisson GLM and model selection 


```{r , echo=FALSE}

summary(species)
##pH (categorical), Biomass (numerical), Species (numerical)

species.glm <- glm(Species ~ Biomass, data = species, family = poisson)

anova(species.glm)
anova(species.glm, test = "Chisq")


##        Df Deviance Resid. Df Resid. Dev  Pr(>Chi)    
##NULL                       89     452.35              
##Biomass  1   44.673        88     407.67 2.328e-11 ***
##---
##Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1'


summary(species.glm)

##Coefficients:
##             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
##(Intercept)  3.184094   0.039159   81.31  < 2e-16 ***
##Biomass     -0.064441   0.009838   -6.55 5.74e-11 ***

speciesph <- factor(species$pH, levels = c("low", "mid", "high"))
##make ph a factor to utilize 

ggplot(species, aes(Biomass,Species, color = speciesph)) + geom_point()

##model selection

s1 <- lm(species$Species ~ 1, family = poisson, data = species)
s2 <- lm(species$Species ~ species$Biomass,family = poisson, data = species)
s3 <- lm(species$Species ~ species$pH,family = poisson, data = species)
s4 <- lm(species$Species ~ species$Biomass * species$pH,family = poisson, data = species)
s5 <- lm(species$Species ~ species$Biomass + species$pH,family = poisson, data = species)

AICc(s1)
AICc(s2)
AICc(s3)
AICc(s4)
AICc(s5)

##[1] 667.1396
##[1] 659.7421
##[1] 622.5944
##[1] 505.7315
##[1] 501.5387

##Model 5 is the lowest AICc number so it is the best fit 

summary(s5)

##Residuals:
##   Min     1Q Median     3Q    Max 
##-8.965 -2.693  0.062  2.171 15.508 

##Coefficients:
##                Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
##(Intercept)      40.2449     1.0923   36.84   <2e-16 ***
##species$Biomass  -2.7276     0.1717  -15.89   <2e-16 ***
##species$pHlow   -22.6200     1.0818  -20.91   <2e-16 ***
##species$pHmid   -10.6418     1.0063  -10.57   <2e-16 ***
##---
##Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

##Residual standard error: 3.783 on 86 degrees of freedom
##Multiple R-squared:  0.8524,	Adjusted R-squared:  0.8472 
##F-statistic: 165.5 on 3 and 86 DF,  p-value: < 2.2e-16

plot(s5)

spred <- predict(s5, type = "response")
ggplot(species, aes(x = species$Biomass, y = species$Species, color = species$pH)) + geom_point() + geom_line(aes(y=spred))

## Species biomass decreases typically alongside pH increasing, across all three species data sets. 


```

## Bolger Regression and Model Selection 

```{r , echo=FALSE}

summary(bolger)

##PERSHRUB (numerical), DISTX (numerical), AGE (numerical), RODENTSP (yes no numerical binary)

cor(bolger[,1:3]) ##quick correlation matrix 
##not sure if the larger or smaller number is better here... probably the larger negative because it's farther away from 1.0? 

b1 <- glm(bolger$RODENTSP ~ 1, family = "binomial", data = bolger)
b2 <- glm(bolger$RODENTSP ~ bolger$PERSHRUB,family = "binomial", data = bolger)
b3 <- glm(bolger$RODENTSP ~ bolger$AGE,family = "binomial", data = bolger)
b4 <- glm(bolger$RODENTSP ~ bolger$DISTX,family = "binomial", data = bolger)
b5 <- glm(bolger$RODENTSP ~ bolger$PERSHRUB * bolger$AGE,family = "binomial", data = bolger)
b6 <- glm(bolger$RODENTSP ~ bolger$PERSHRUB + bolger$AGE,family = "binomial", data = bolger)
b7 <- glm(bolger$RODENTSP ~ bolger$PERSHRUB * bolger$DISTX,family = "binomial", data = bolger)
b8 <- glm(bolger$RODENTSP ~ bolger$PERSHRUB + bolger$DISTX,family = "binomial", data = bolger)
b9 <- glm(bolger$RODENTSP ~ bolger$PERSHRUB * bolger$AGE * bolger$DISTX,family = "binomial", data = bolger)
b10 <- glm(bolger$RODENTSP ~ bolger$PERSHRUB + bolger$AGE + bolger$DISTX,family = "binomial", data = bolger)

AIC(b1)
AIC(b2)
AIC(b3)
AIC(b4)
AIC(b5)
AIC(b6)
AIC(b7)
AIC(b8)
AIC(b9)
AIC(b10)

##b2 folloed by b6 are best models


summary(b2)

##Coefficients:
##                Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
##(Intercept)     -0.116055   0.149728  -0.775 0.446172    
##bolger$PERSHRUB  0.012135   0.002636   4.603 0.000125 ***
##---
##Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
##
##(Dispersion parameter for gaussian family taken to be 0.1412207)
##
##    Null deviance: 6.2400  on 24  degrees of freedom
##Residual deviance: 3.2481  on 23  degrees of freedom
##AIC: 25.927
##
##Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 2

b2 <- glm(bolger$RODENTSP ~ bolger$PERSHRUB, family = binomial, data=bolger)

bpred <- predict(b2, type = "response")
ggplot(bolger, aes(x = PERSHRUB, y = RODENTSP,  ylab = "Rodent Present", xlab = "Per Shrub")) + geom_point() + geom_line(aes(y=bpred), color = "blue")

##Bolger was present yes or no based on number of shrubs, more likely to have been yes, found, at higher per shrub counts. 

```

## Molerat GammaGLM 

```{r , echo=FALSE}

summary(molerat)
show(molerat)

## caste (categorical), lnmass (numerical), lnenergy (numerical)

moleratcaste <- factor(molerat$caste, levels = "worker", "lazy")

hist(molerat$lnenergy)
hist(molerat$lnmass)

ggplot(molerat, aes(molerat$lnmass, molerat$lnenergy, color = molerat$caste)) + geom_point()

##Larger molerat mass trends to being lazy rather than a worker 

gamma <- Gamma(link = "log")
##use a log link

m1 <- glm(molerat$lnenergy ~ 1, family = Gamma(link = "log"))
m2 <- glm(molerat$lnenergy ~ molerat$lnmass,family = Gamma(link = "log"))
m3 <- glm(molerat$lnenergy ~ molerat$caste,family = Gamma(link = "log"))
m4 <- glm(molerat$lnenergy ~ molerat$lnmass * molerat$caste,family = Gamma(link = "log"))
m5 <- glm(molerat$lnenergy ~ molerat$lnmass + molerat$caste,family = Gamma(link = "log"))

AIC(m1)
AIC(m2)
AIC(m3)
AIC(m4)
AIC(m5)

##[1] 33.04415
##[1] 23.57633
##[1] 34.54878
##[1] 19.83
##[1] 18.79253

##Model 5 is best with lowest number, followed by 4

summary(m5)

##Coefficients:
##                    Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
##(Intercept)         -0.09687    0.94230  -0.103   0.9188    
##molerat$lnmass       0.89282    0.19303   4.625 5.89e-05 ***
##molerat$casteworker  0.39334    0.14611   2.692   0.0112 *  
##---
##Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
##
##(Dispersion parameter for gaussian family taken to be 0.08795314)
##
##    Null deviance: 4.7626  on 34  degrees of freedom
##Residual deviance: 2.8145  on 32  degrees of freedom
##AIC: 19.106
##Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 2

moleratpred <- predict(m5, type = "response")
ggplot(molerat, aes(molerat$lnmass, molerat$lnenergy, color = molerat$caste)) + geom_point() + geom_line(aes(y=moleratpred))

##Energy in molerats increases as mass increases, but also as mass increases the likelihood that the molerat is lazy increases, as higher mass correlates to lazyness despite higher energy 

```
Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
